checked: The Civil Service Commission's 2026 CSE-PPT announcement lists Environment Management and Protection under General Information: https://csc.gov.ph/phocadownload/userupload/erpo/announcements/2026/ExamAnn_2026_03_Conduct%20of%2009%20Aug%202026%20CSE-PPT_orig%20signed.pdf

RA 9003 supports source segregation, the four named waste categories, and waste diversion through source reduction, reuse, recycling, and composting: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html

EMB guidance defines the ECC as a decision document after EIA review and states that covered projects require the EIA/ECC process before implementation: https://eia.emb.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/eia-ecc.pdf

PD 1586 establishes the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System and requires an ECC for declared environmentally critical projects or areas: https://issuances-library.senate.gov.ph/legislative%2Bissuances/Presidential%20Decree%20No.%201586%2C%20s.%201978

RA 10121 establishes a proactive, comprehensive DRRM system spanning prevention or mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery or rehabilitation: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2010/ra_10121_2010.html
Checked the four Core Concept factual claims in the audited lesson text against those primary sources.
Solved Example 1 from the question alone: the household separates waste where it is generated, so my answer is segregation at source; this matches the lesson.
Solved Example 2 from the question alone: composting keeps material out of disposal facilities, so my answer is waste diversion; this matches the lesson.

Solved Example 3 from the question alone: a project already stated to be covered by the Philippine EIS System must secure an Environmental Compliance Certificate before implementation; this matches the lesson.
